project.projectDesc: Combines real-time patient events and batch bed-configuration data to support hospital bed visibility and capacity forecasts.

caseStudy.summary: This hospital-operations platform combines real-time HL7 events with batch bed-configuration data to support inpatient bed visibility and forecasting. I contributed streaming and batch data pipelines, historical snapshots, and ARIMA-based capacity forecasting.
caseStudy.challenge: Hospital bed state and patient movement change continuously, while configuration and historical context arrive through separate data processes. The system needed both timely event processing and durable history to support operational analysis and forecasts.
caseStudy.architecture: HL7 patient events are processed through a streaming path, while Airflow jobs ingest bed configurations and create historical snapshots. The resulting data supports bed-state analysis and ARIMA time-series forecasts of inpatient availability.
caseStudy.diagram:
flowchart LR
  HL7[HL7 patient events] --> Stream[AWS streaming processor]
  Config[Bed configuration data] --> Airflow[Airflow batch jobs]
  Stream --> Snapshots[Historical snapshots]
  Airflow --> Snapshots
  Snapshots --> Store[Operational data store]
  Store --> Forecast[ARIMA capacity forecasts]
  Forecast --> Hospital[Hospital operations teams]
contributions: Designed and contributed to a lambda architecture combining real-time events and batch processing.
Built real-time processing for HL7 patient activity transitions.
Developed Airflow jobs for bed configuration ingestion and historical snapshots.
Supported ARIMA forecasting of inpatient bed availability and patient-flow patterns.
Modified processing logic to meet evolving data-science requirements.
tradeoffs: Combining streaming and batch processing provides freshness and historical context, but requires reconciliation across both paths.
Historical snapshots make trend analysis possible while increasing storage and data-quality responsibilities.
Forecasts complement operational visibility; they should not be treated as substitutes for hospital staff judgment.

business: Bed-state visibility and capacity forecasts support hospital planning.
quality: Historical snapshots provide a time-series foundation for analyzing bed availability.
